title: Opinion Language and Stance
text:
When writers present an opinion, they often use language that shows how certain they are. Phrases such as 'I strongly believe' signal confidence, while 'it seems likely' suggests caution. Readers who notice these signals can better judge how much weight to give an argument. Stance language therefore plays an important role in persuasive writing.

Some writers, however, hide their opinions behind neutral words. A phrase such as 'many people say' makes a claim sound more general than it really is. Careful readers should ask who is actually making the claim. Recognizing these subtle choices helps them separate facts from personal judgments.

questions.text: According to the first paragraph, what does the phrase 'I strongly believe' signal?
According to the second paragraph, what effect does the phrase 'many people say' have?
options: It makes a claim sound more general than it is
It makes a claim sound more personal
It proves that a claim is true
It shows the writer is certain

questions.text: What can the reader infer from the first paragraph about persuasive writing?
options: Stance language does not affect how readers judge arguments
Readers can judge arguments more fairly when they notice stance language
Writers should avoid expressing any opinion
Only academic writers use stance language

questions.text: What is the writer's main advice to careful readers in the second paragraph?
options: Accept every claim that uses neutral words
Ask who is actually making a claim

vocabulary.definition: intended to convince people to accept an opinion or argument
to show or indicate something, often without saying it directly
not showing support for either side of an opinion
small or difficult to notice, but still important

paragraph_translations: Kiedy autorzy przedstawiają swoją opinię, często używają języka, który pokazuje, jak bardzo są pewni swoich słów. Zwroty takie jak 'I strongly believe' sygnalizują pewność, a 'it seems likely' sugeruje ostrożność. Czytelnicy, którzy zauważają te sygnały, lepiej oceniają, jaką wagę przykładać do argumentu. Język wyrażania stanowiska odgrywa zatem ważną rolę w perswazyjnym pisaniu.

Niektórzy autorzy jednak ukrywają swoje opinie za neutralnymi słowami. Zwrot taki jak 'many people say' sprawia, że twierdzenie brzmi bardziej ogólnie, niż jest w rzeczywistości. Uważni czytelnicy powinni zapytać, kto tak naprawdę wysuwa dane twierdzenie. Rozpoznawanie tych subtelnych wyborów pomaga im oddzielać fakty od osobistych ocen.
